text: When this chapter is set beside the earlier promise, the difference between them narrows. Isaac is recalled to the reader as the child of the covenant, the son through whom the nations are to be blessed; and that promise, so recalled, is made the matter of a test. The whole scene turns upon a single word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times, once to God, once to Isaac, and once to the angel. The word never bears the same meaning twice, and the price of saying it is greater with every repetition; so that Abraham cannot be present, either to God or to his son, without some loss in being so.
